newsitem.title: UK: Round-the-world walker confesses to fraud.
newsitem.headline: Round-the-world walker confesses to fraud.

text.p: A British woman who spent 11 years setting a record as the first woman to walk around the world has admitted she cheated.
Ffyona Campbell, who left home at the age of 16 on her global trek, said she skipped 1,000 miles (1,600 km) of her walk across the United States.
Campbell, 29, told British newspapers and television that her punishing regime of 25 miles (40 km) a day was too much.
"I shouldn't be remembered as the first woman to walk around the world when I cheated. I broke the unwritten rule of the Guinness Book of Records," she told Independent Television News.
Campbell said she rode in her support truck for the leg between Indianapolis and Fort Summer, New Mexico.
"I got into the back of the vehicle and drove ahead and didn't drive back to continue walking properly," she said.
She completed her walk in Scotland to cheering crowds in 1994. "They were walking beside me as a role model. They were respecting me. To them I owe the biggest apology."
Campbell's round-the-world walk began in September 1983 when she walked from the northern tip of Scotland to Land's End -- the farthest southwest tip of England -- in 49 days.

In the spring of 1985 Campbell, then 18, walked the 3,500 miles (5,600 km) from New York to Los Angeles in 151 days. She crossed the 3,200 miles (5,150 km) between Sydney and Perth in 95 days in 1988.
Campbell started walking from Cape Town to Tangiers in April 1991. She walked from Algeciras, Spain, to Calais, France and then back to Britain in 1994.
